problem: Embodied AI lacks internet-scale vision-action pretraining data because real robot trajectories are costly. Prior desktop or game efforts are domain-specific (VPT for Minecraft) or proprietary (SIMA), and there is no standard toolkit or verified transfer to robotics.
motivation: Desktop and gaming interactions (screen, keyboard, mouse) are abundant and tightly couple observation and action. Their cheap collection, together with pseudo-labeling of unlabeled YouTube gameplay, could give a scalable pretraining substrate that transfers to physical manipulation and navigation.
key_idea: Collect and standardize desktop gameplay data with the OWA Toolkit, train a timestamp-based Generalist inverse dynamics model (NEP-tau) to pseudo-label 1K+ hours of YouTube gameplay, and use the data for vision-action pretraining (VAPT) of InternVL3-1B that transfers to robot manipulation and navigation.
insight: Future observation context is essential for the IDM: the tau=0 ablation collapses Pearson correlation to about 0.1, and performance stabilizes for tau>=100 ms. Desktop pretraining helps downstream: LIBERO-10 rises from 54.2 to 93.6 and training loss shows no initial plateau. Pseudo-labeled data helps navigation (CANVAS 75.3 to 83.3), where high-level planning matters, but does not help or slightly hurts manipulation (LIBERO 96.6 to 92.2), where precise human supervision matters more.
method: OWA Toolkit / ocap: a Windows recorder (DXGI, GStreamer, H.265) that captures synchronized screen, keyboard, mouse and audio at FHD/QHD 60 Hz, stored in the MCAP-based OWAMcap format (152x compression on VPT data) with MediaRef video references.
Optimized data pipeline: fixed-GOP x264 without B-frames, FSLDataset packing episodes into fixed-length sequences, and adaptive batch decoding (10.2x throughput, 41x less disk read than TorchCodec).
Timestamp-based event tokenization: screen, keyboard and mouse events serialized as <EVENT_START>{TYPE}{TIMESTAMP}{DETAIL}<EVENT_END> with digit tokens (10 ms resolution), avoiding no-op ticks.

Generalist-IDM with NEP-tau: InternVL3-1B trained with next-event prediction where observations are shifted by tau=100 ms to expose future frames; streaming autoregressive inference with a temporal stopping criterion and sliding context.
Pseudo-labeling: 1054.8 h of 480p YouTube 'no commentary' gameplay across 20 games labeled by the G-IDM, added to 259 h of human data.

VAPT: InternVL3-1B pretrained on desktop vision-action data (1 epoch on pseudo-labeled, then 3 epochs on human data), then fine-tuned on downstream tasks (OpenVLA-OFT-style head for LIBERO, SmolVLA protocol for Meta-World/SO101, CANVAS waypoint tokens for navigation).

setting.training_data: 259 h human desktop gameplay across 20 games (335.6 h collected in total), plus 1054.8 h of YouTube gameplay pseudo-labeled by the G-IDM; the IDM is also trained on the human data; downstream fine-tuning on LIBERO, Meta-World, SO101 (208 demos) and the CANVAS COMMAND dataset
setting.observation: CANVAS: egocentric RGB with instruction; LIBERO: third-person + wrist RGB, proprioception, language; pretraining: screen frames
setting.action_space: LIBERO: continuous actions via L1 regression head with chunk size 8; CANVAS: waypoint tokens (128); pretraining: keyboard/mouse events
setting.simulator: LIBERO, Meta-World, CANVAS simulation; real SO101 arm

numbers.extra: pretrained on 259 h human plus 1K+ h pseudo-labeled desktop data; fine-tuned on the COMMAND dataset; 3 repeats with random orientations
numbers.evidence: Table canvas_results: Total 83.3 for + VAPT w/ pseudo

numbers.extra: OpenVLA-OFT-style head, LoRA rank 32; no robotics VLA pretraining

numbers_note: Benchmarks are not navigation-VLN benchmarks; the CANVAS sim navigation results are the only navigation numbers. The CANVAS per-scene breakdown is omitted.
results: A 1B VAPT model reaches 96.6% on LIBERO (up from 84.8% for the InternVL3-1B baseline), matching or beating pi0 (86.0), OpenVLA (76.5) and SmolVLA (88.7); it is below OpenVLA-OFT (97.1). On CANVAS navigation, pseudo-labeled pretraining gives 83.3% vs 75.3% for the baseline. The G-IDM also beats per-game Specialist IDMs in-distribution and on unseen games.
limitations: Real-world evaluation is a single pick-and-place task on one arm.
Pseudo-labels help navigation but hurt manipulation, and the mechanism is not understood.
Data is mainly gameplay and may not cover the desktop activities relevant to general robotics; evaluation covers only small benchmarks with limited seeds and episodes.
